e6:CWO18-NEARWEB-1#1.decision: A span that matches WEB text once case and punctuation are folded is a WEB QUOTATION CARRIED INEXACTLY, not a gloss, and is a CWO-EZ-18 (ii) author item; the literal reading of (i) ('found nowhere in the WEB') is not applied to it. Basis on the bytes of Ezek_web_clean.txt (a7e59bcb): WEB 8:6 ends 'But you will again see yet other great abominations.”' and P02-001 writes “you will again see yet other great abominations,” - the verse's words with a trailing comma for its period; 8:7 opens 'He brought me to the door of the court;' and P02-002 writes “he brought me to the door of the court” - sentence-initial case; 8:8 'Son of man, dig now in the wall.' against “son of man, dig now in the wall”; 9:11 'I have done as you have commanded me.”' against “I have done as you have commanded me,”; 10:9 'The appearance of the wheels was like a beryl stone.' against “the appearance of the wheels was like a beryl stone”; 11:6 'You have multiplied your slain' against “you have multiplied your slain” (P02-008 refs[1]). Each is the verse's own wording with one edit at the edge of the quotation; a reader takes it as WEB text, which is exactly what C3's curly form asserts, and converting it to single quotes would hide a WEB quotation as a gloss and remove it from check_web_quotes' view for good. This is ruled from the words and the matcher's folded outcome, not from translation punctuation alone (E-23): the case or punctuation difference is what the author repairs, never what decides the class. ROUTING: the 26 prose spans in near_web_glosses.items and the 4 outside-prose folded spans (CWO18-SCOPE-1) are author items - 30 in all - and the remedy is either (a) restore the span VERBATIM to the WEB bytes (case and punctuation; a quotation's edge punctuation goes outside the closing quote where the row's sentence needs its own) and add the inline web: ref - the analysis names one verse for 17 of the 26 prose spans and for all 4 outside-prose spans, and for the nine folded in several verses ('then you will know that I am Yahweh' x4, 17 verses; 'Set your face', 11; 'it will happen in that day', 3; 'your nation,', 3; 'out of their own heart.', 2; 'or if…', 2) the author names the verse the row means, which the row's span or its oshb: refs already identify - or (b) rewrite it as a gloss in single quotes. The remaining 21 prose glosses (the dry run's 47 minus these 26) convert under (i) as ruled: each is found nowhere in the WEB under either matcher (among them the quoted OSHB note text at P08-002, the rows' own labels such as “row or texture”, “two-sided unit”, “a seam is assessed from both sides”, and glosses such as “lift up your eyes / do you see”). The deterministic script implements 'near-WEB' exactly as the analysis measured it: fold = norm_english, then lowercase, every non-alphanumeric character to a space, whitespace collapsed; a span is near-WEB when ' ' + fold(span) + ' ' is a substring of the folded text of all 1,273 verses joined in canonical order; the amended dry run must reproduce the 26 + 4.
e6:CWO18-NEARWEB-1#1.reason: The order's (i)/(ii) split rests on whether a span IS WEB text; a span that is a verse's words with its first letter lowercased for the row's sentence is WEB text carried inexactly, and the only honest forms are the verbatim quotation with its ref or a declared gloss. Deciding the class from the words rather than the punctuation is what E-23 requires; the punctuation is the repair. The 21 residual glosses are safe to convert because neither the exact nor the folded matcher finds them, which is the (i) condition in both its readings.

e6:CWO18-SHORT-1#1.decision: ADOPTED with four changes. A span of three words or fewer (whitespace-split after strip) that stands verbatim, case-exact, in two or more WEB verses (web_quote_found over each verse's own text, counted per verse) is a LABEL - a formula, epithet or place name the row uses as a name, not a quotation of one verse - and converts deterministically to single quotes with the same manifest assertions as a gloss. Basis on the rows' bytes (rows_v3_cwo13.jsonl 324d2358): the P08 rows write 'oath formula (“As I live”)' in prose and refs alike and 'the “behold, I am against you” verdict-onset device'; P02-011 and P02-012 write 'an infixed “in the morning” phrase' and 'the infixed “in the morning” word-event re-onset' of MT 12:8, whose WEB text reads 'In the morning, Yahweh’s word came to me' - 12:8 is not even among the two verses the case-exact matcher found for the lowercase span (24:18, 33:22), so the span names a device rather than quoting a verse; single quotes are the tools' own idiom for a gloss or label (check_web_quotes lines 189-191: 'Glosses - the legitimate single-curly idiom'). This is ruled from the bytes and the matcher's per-verse counts, not from translation punctuation (E-23), and it weakens neither CWO-EZ-18's coverage condition (the class still reads 0 over the applied rows) nor any HARD gate (check_web_quotes is a FLAGS member). CHANGES: (1) the threshold is exactly as proposed and is NOT widened to longer spans: a longer span verbatim in several verses can be a quotation of the one verse the row means with another verse's case - “behold, I am against you” is verbatim in 13:8 and 29:10 while P08-007 means 35:3, whose WEB text reads 'Behold, I am against you, Mount Seir' - and that is the author's to resolve under (ii); (2) the manifest records converted labels under their own class ('short_common_label'), never among the glosses, each with its per-verse count and the verse keys; (3) every converted label is listed to its part's FIXUP-1 author as an INFORMATIONAL item requiring no action: 'converted to a single-quoted label; if a quotation of one verse was meant, restore the curly form with the inline web: ref' - P02-002's “in the dark,” (WEB 8:12, standing beside its sibling author item “Yahweh doesn’t see us”) is the case this protects; (4) the rule applies in every field in scope (CWO18-SCOPE-1), which adds the 11 outside-prose labels enumerated there to the 34 prose labels in routed_ii.short_common_items (45 labels in all). The 37 remaining prose (ii) spans and the 11 outside-prose verbatim spans stay author items. A span of three words or fewer found in exactly one verse ('one heart', 11:19; 'Yahweh doesn’t see us' is four words) stays (ii).
e6:CWO18-SHORT-1#1.reason: The matcher can name no source verse for a two- or three-word span that a book of formulae writes dozens of times ('Son of man' 61 verses, 'son of man' 34, 'the nations' 68, 'the land' 114, 'As I live' 10, 'river Chebar' 8), and the rows use these as names of devices, which is what the rows' own wording ('oath formula', 'verdict-onset device', 'infixed phrase') shows; routing 45 such spans to authors would buy 45 'drop the quotes' edits and nothing else. The threshold is kept narrow because 'behold, I am against you' shows how a longer verbatim-in-several-verses span can still be one verse's quotation in disguise. The informational listing costs nothing and keeps the one plausible loss ('in the dark,') in the author's hands.
